The build is green.

## Summary

The spec required all rejection responses (400, 409, 429) to return an RFC7807 `application/problem+json` body containing `type`, `title`, `status`, and `detail`.

Nine escalation handlers were still returning a plain `application/json` `{"errors": [...]}` map body. I converted each to build an RFC7807 `ProblemDetail` via the existing `ProblemDetails.build(...)` helper (which sets `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, plus a timestamp) and send it as `ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail>` — the same pattern the already-compliant `ValidationExceptionHandler`/`DataIntegrityViolationExceptionHandler` use, so Spring emits the `application/problem+json` content type. Status codes are unchanged:

- **400** — `DisposableEmailDomain`, `FutureRegistrationDate`, `InvalidEmail`, `InvalidPostcode`, `InvalidTelephone`, `MissingOwnerFields`
- **409** — `CityAtCapacity`, `DuplicateIdentity`
- **429** — `DailyLimitExceeded`

## Summary

The spec required all rejection responses (400, 409, 429) to return an RFC7807 `application/problem+json` body containing `type`, `title`, `status`, and `detail`.

Nine escalation handlers were still returning a plain `application/json` `{"errors": [...]}` map body. I converted each to build an RFC7807 `ProblemDetail` via the existing `ProblemDetails.build(...)` helper (which sets `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, plus a timestamp) and send it as `ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail>` — the same pattern the already-compliant `ValidationExceptionHandler`/`DataIntegrityViolationExceptionHandler` use, so Spring emits the `application/problem+json` content type. - **409** — `CityAtCapacity`, `DuplicateIdentity`
- **429** — `DailyLimitExceeded`
